column1: ONS/2026-11-17-labour-market-overview-uk-november-2026.md|||ONS UK labour market overview, November 2026: vacancies down 22,000 to 690,000 (Aug to Oct), with the smallest firms at 73,000, their lowest outside the pandemic since 2012; payrolled employees down 95,000 on the year in the October flash; unemployment 4.6% and employment 75.4% (partly a survey rotation effect); regular pay growth slowed to 3.5%.|||ONS|||hiring volume, uk data, compensation benchmarks, by industry, by company size, workforce planning, trends / predictions

CIPD/2026-11-12-labour-market-outlook-autumn-2026.md|||CIPD Labour Market Outlook autumn 2026 (YouGov, 2,051 UK employers): net employment balance +10, subdued for a seventh quarter; 62% plan to recruit (58% private sector); 30% have hard-to-fill vacancies; expected pay awards 3%; 83% have adopted AI but only 8% deeply; 25% of AI-using employers expect AI to cut headcount in the next year, up from 21%.|||CIPD|||hiring volume, uk data, compensation benchmarks, ai adoption, by industry, by company size, workforce planning, survey, trends / predictions

Korn Ferry/2026-10-22-talent-trends-2027-skills-shifting.md|||Korn Ferry's 13th annual Talent Trends report (1,300+ talent and senior leaders, 75+ countries): 77% say capability gaps will outweigh talent shortages in 2027; adaptability ranked the top skill; 40% will hold entry-level volumes but redesign the roles while 19% cut and lean on AI; only 6% think senior leaders are ready for AI change; 69% expect HR, TA, L&D and workforce planning to merge.|||Korn Ferry|||skills-based hiring, early career talent, ai adoption, human-ai collaboration, internal mobility, workforce planning, global data, survey, trends / predictions

iCIMS/2026-11-10-workforce-report-november-2026.md|||iCIMS November 2026 Workforce Report: US hires 1% below last October while openings sit 7% above; EMEA applications up 9% and openings up 2% but hires 18% down; time to fill near 39 days; 51% of 1,000 US job seekers met a multistep AI-led process with little human contact and only 32% were told AI was used; 500 HR leaders use on average 52% of the AI they bought.|||iCIMS|||hiring volume, time to fill, applications per hire, candidate experience, ai adoption, ai governance, us data, emea data, product data study, survey

TestGorilla/2026-09-30-recruiting-in-the-ai-era-2026.md|||TestGorilla survey of 1,428 US and 483 UK talent professionals: AI made sourcing faster for 72% US but only 58% UK, and surer for 59% US and 48% UK; 75% of UK recruiters think AI wrote at least half the CVs they see; verifying CV skills is the top sourcing challenge (57% US, 49% UK); 69% still review 26+ profiles per contact; 73% UK spend an hour or more checking one candidate.|||TestGorilla|||ai sourcing, candidate fraud, skills-based hiring, recruiter productivity, quality of hire, rec tech, uk data, us data, survey
